# Reliability

Failure modes, and the mechanisms that address them with their parameters.

7 unit(s). `Stages` is the maturity range where a concept applies — an agent filters on it so that concepts from a larger system than yours are not offered.

| Concept | Stages | Cost | What it is |
| :-- | :-- | --: | :-- |
| [Availability Targets](availability-targets.md) | 1,2,3,4,5 | 0 | Translating an availability target into permitted downtime and then into the mechanisms it requires, and refusing targets the architecture cannot deliver. |
| [Bulkheads](bulkheads.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 0 | Isolating resource pools per dependency so that one slow dependency cannot consume the capacity every other request path needs. |
| [Circuit Breakers](circuit-breakers.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 1 | Failing fast against a dependency that is already failing, so that a sustained outage does not consume the caller's capacity and does not prolong the dependency's recovery. |
| [Failure Mode Analysis](failure-mode-analysis.md) | 1,2,3,4,5 | 0 | Nine structured questions asked of every component and dependency edge, so that failure reasoning is exhaustive rather than dependent on what the reviewer happens to think of. |
| [Graceful Degradation](graceful-degradation.md) | 2,3,4,5 | 0 | Deciding in advance which features degrade and to what, so that a partial failure produces a reduced service rather than an error page. |
| [Retries, Backoff and Jitter](retries-backoff-jitter.md) | 1,2,3,4,5 | 0 | Retrying only idempotent operations, with exponential backoff and randomised jitter, so that recovery attempts do not amplify the outage they are responding to. |
| [Timeouts](timeouts.md) | 0,1,2,3,4,5 | 0 | Every outbound call needs an explicit connect and read timeout derived from the caller's own latency budget; a dependency that becomes slow without failing is the usual cause of a total outage. |

`Cost` is the complexity points a concept adds if adopted; 0 means it is a technique rather than a component. See `frameworks/complexity-budget/`.
